chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan عليه السلام about ghusl on Friday, al-Adha, and al-Fitr. He said: It is a sunnah, not an obligation.

key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: Eid al-Adha, the festival of sacrifice
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fitr, the festival marking the end of fasting
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended practice established in the religious tradition

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl on Friday and the two Eids obligatory or recommended in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that ghusl for Friday, Eid al-Adha, and Eid al-Fitr is recommended rather than obligatory. It serves as a legal indication in ritual purity and devotional practice that these baths are from the sunnah and not a binding duty.
